Between those events, a selection expansion, caret move or policy revision can make the already painted text inapplicable.

A client may preserve a remaining suggestion after the developer types a matching prefix only by explicitly rebasing the remainder to the new version and range. Otherwise invalidate it. Returning to the same visible caret does not revive an earlier epoch. The actual local accept helper models the gate; it does not execute a real editor’s atomic edit API.

A useful latency measurement begins with the qualifying edit and ends when a fresh span is painted. Include local handling, network, context assembly, queueing, enough generation to display and rendering. Our immediate-trigger worksheet totals less than the scenario’s two-hundred-millisecond objective.

Add the separate ordinary-typing debounce and the same serial path now exceeds that allocation. Shorten it, route locally or define a different pause-to-suggestion objective. Compute real percentiles over complete request traces, with stale drops and timeouts visible, instead of adding stage percentiles together.

Add the immediate serial allocations: twelve client, fifty-five network, twenty-eight context, seventy-eight queue and model through a usable span, and ten paint. The total is one hundred eighty-three milliseconds, leaving seventeen against the supplied two-hundred target. Adding ordinary typing’s one hundred fifty debounce gives three hundred thirty-three. A budget allocation is not an observed percentile.

The executed counterexample has twenty complete requests: one with stages one hundred and one, another with one and one hundred, and eighteen with one and one. Nearest-rank p ninety-five selects rank nineteen. Complete sums have p ninety-five of one hundred one, but each stage’s p ninety-five is one, so summing those percentiles gives two. Preserve row identity before adding stages and sorting requests.

Edit-to-usable-suggestion begins at the qualifying event and ends with a fresh displayed span. Client TTFT begins at request submission and ends with the first token received; it already contains transport and server waiting within that interval. Do not add TTFT to its own component stages. Generating one token may also be insufficient for the span the product displays.

Report the population behind latency percentiles. Timeouts, errors, cancellations and stale drops must stay visible, even when they produce no displayed completion. A low tail among a small surviving shown subset can coexist with poor service. Separate the ordinary-typing pause objective from immediate triggers instead of silently starting both clocks at HTTP submission.

Consecutive edits often preserve the same file header. Compatible prefix caching can reuse its earlier key and value computation, leaving only the changed input delta to prefill. Exact token prefixes, model configuration and authenticated tenant scope determine whether that reuse is permitted.

The hit still generates the new suggestion. In our supplied service times, decode stays unchanged while prefill falls. Editing near the top invalidates later cached states, and another tenant is a miss by design. Neither prefix reuse nor response caching can bypass the current editor snapshot.

The actual contract fixture keys security scope, model revision, tokenizer revision, adapter revision, KV layout and exact prefix IDs. Security scope comes from authenticated tenant, repository access and policy epoch. The same key hits; a different tenant, final ID, adapter or policy does not. This Python tuple and illustrative handle do not implement a real KV allocator or vLLM’s block hash.

vLLM’s documented full-block hashes include parent context and block token IDs, plus extra hashes such as adapter identity and cache salt. The salt can partition trust groups but must not be accepted as authority chosen by an arbitrary client. Cache permissions and current repository access still precede reuse. Exact visible source text alone can hide changed framing, retrieved content or tokenization.

KV reuse removes repeated prefill, not computation for a new generated answer. A response cache has a different contract including the full input, generation settings, model and policy. Neither cache overrides freshness at paint or insertion. Reusing a computation and reusing a finished suggestion must remain separately observable.

The article’s complete prompt has twelve hundred reusable header tokens and eighty new input tokens. Supplied model-service times are seventy-two prefill plus twenty-four decode on a miss, and eleven plus the same twenty-four on a hit: ninety-six versus thirty-five milliseconds. These omit queueing, network and paint and are not TTFT measurements.

Change an early prefix token in PSM and later suffix states also depend on that changed context. A supported suffix-first SPM format can retain earlier suffix KV while a prefix grows; changing the suffix instead invalidates later prefix state. Count exact full blocks after real tokenization, under compatible positions and layout. Routing to a cold replica can still remove a logically possible hit.

In the five-token toy draft, graph, dot, allows, opening parenthesis and user are separate IDs. The first four survive and request replaces user, giving five emitted tokens. One accepted draft gives two with correction; immediate rejection still emits one. All five accepted may add a sixth target bonus, subject to stopping rules. The correction is emitted without its own target KV. When generation continues, the next target forward pass processes that token and computes its KV. Discard target KV states for the rejected draft token and any later draft tokens.

For stochastic verification over the same vocabulary, accept a proposed token with the smaller of one and target probability divided by draft probability. On rejection, subtract draft from target coordinate by coordinate, clamp negatives to zero and normalize the remainder. Greedy verification instead uses target greedy choices. A confidence cutoff cannot substitute for the specified probability rule.

The worksheet assumes five draft steps cost one ordinary target step and verification costs one more. Five emitted outputs for cost two gives two point five outputs per baseline cost, under those invented costs. Actual verification processes multiple target positions; at high occupancy it can take work from neighboring requests. Measure first-token and complete latency as well as accepted length.

The executed selection fixture requires mean accepted draft length at least two and latency gain at least ten milliseconds. Python imports supplies three point eight and a forty-two-millisecond gain, from one hundred seventy-eight to one hundred thirty-six. SQL supplies one point one and loses seven, from one hundred sixty-nine to one hundred seventy-six. Only the Python fixture passes both conditions.

These inputs are invented and the rule is a local selection check. A release also needs compatible greedy or stochastic behavior, correct completions, failure rates, representative arrival load and enough observations for tails. Boilerplate may raise draft agreement for a slice; that remains a hypothesis to test rather than a property of every code language.

Raw eight-bit weights take half the payload of sixteen-bit weights; four-bit takes a quarter. For a hypothetical three-billion-weight array, sixteen bits use six decimal gigabytes and four bits use one point five. Scales, metadata, unquantized layers, KV and temporary buffers remain outside that arithmetic. GPTQ is post-training weight quantization, not new infill training.

Efficient kernels can reduce bandwidth-bound decode traffic, while unsupported formats or other bottlenecks can remove a speed benefit. Profile prefill and decode separately and admit enough memory for the actual KV batch. Recheck syntax, insecure API behavior, acceptance, retained text and latency by language and suggestion type. Fitting compressed weights does not establish a useful editor response.

A developer is shown four suggestions. Follow what happens after each acceptance. The first is accepted, then entirely removed. The second stays as accepted. The third is partly edited, and the fourth is never accepted. Watch the totals accumulate. Count distinct accepted suggestions separately from inserted characters and characters retained after a chosen observation window.

These editing signals complement correctness checks. A retained permission bug is still a bug, while missing observation windows remain censored. Keep trigger and display policy fixed when comparing candidates, and measure useful edits, shown rate, stale drops and latency by language and suggestion type.

For the four shown IDs, three have inserted text, so acceptance is three divided by four, or seventy-five percent. Inserted characters total eighteen plus four plus forty-two, or sixty-four; retained original characters total zero plus four plus thirty-five, or thirty-nine. Retained-character rate is thirty-nine divided by sixty-four, about sixty point nine percent. A new replacement character is not a retained original character.

Generalize the denominators: count distinct shown suggestion IDs with any insertion divided by distinct shown IDs. Count retained original characters divided by actually inserted characters for a declared observed window. Repeated partial-accept actions on one ID count one accepted suggestion. With no shown suggestions or no inserted characters, the corresponding rate is undefined; unobserved windows are censored rather than automatically deleted.

The early twenty-twenty-two Copilot study reported twenty-seven-percent acceptance and an observational association with perceived productivity. Acceptance correlated more strongly than persistence in that studied cohort, with unexplained variance. Our retention fixture complements that signal; it does not prove retention causes productivity or that retained permission code is correct. Shown rate and review quality still matter.

For offline evaluation, freeze a real edit point, hide its target insertion and retrieve only files available at that time. Split by repository and time where possible to reduce duplicate leakage. Check parse behavior, relevant tests in an isolated no-secret environment and explicit permission policy. Exact-string scoring can reject valid alternatives; a standard coding benchmark does not exercise IDE timing or display behavior.

For online comparison, randomize at a stable user or workspace boundary and hold trigger and display policy fixed. Compare eligible, requested, shown, accepted and retained populations; retain latency, cancellations, stale drops and errors. Slice by language and suggestion class so aggregate gains cannot hide a broken supported workflow.

Use predefined rollback guardrails with adequate observations and preserve a known-good route for each slice. A model that shows only tiny obvious tokens can raise acceptance while reducing useful work. A model that abstains heavily can improve shown-only accuracy while failing users. Report cost per accepted-and-retained suggestion alongside correctness and coverage, not request count alone.

The article’s peak-hour worksheet begins with five thousand actively typing editors at point four remote requests per second: two thousand raw requests per second. Sixty percent cancel before GPU admission, leaving eight hundred. A cancellation after admission still burns partial work and cannot be subtracted as free. Active editors are not idle logged-in sessions.

Every surviving request in this first worksheet has two thousand forty-eight prompt tokens. Half hit and skip three quarters of prefill; misses keep all work. Remaining work fraction is one half times one quarter plus one half, or point six two five. Eight hundred times two thousand forty-eight times that fraction is one million twenty-four thousand prefill tokens per second.

Dividing by the assumed twenty thousand effective prefill tokens per GPU-second gives fifty-one point two, rounded up to fifty-two worksheet GPUs. It omits decode, late-cancel work, KV capacity, imbalance, failover and headroom. Sequence lengths change token work, so this prefill envelope does not choose an actual GPU fleet or establish the inline p ninety-five.

Keep eight hundred requests, overall mean two thousand forty-eight and fifty-percent request hits, but make the four hundred hits length three thousand seventy-two and misses length one thousand twenty-four. Hits contribute three hundred seven thousand two hundred remaining tokens per second; misses contribute four hundred nine thousand six hundred. The sum is seven hundred sixteen thousand eight hundred, or thirty-six worksheet GPUs.

Swap those lengths between groups. Remaining prefill becomes one million three hundred thirty-one thousand two hundred, or sixty-seven GPUs at the same assumed rate. The equal-length case gave fifty-two. These distributions share the same overall mean and request hit rate; cacheable length and hits are correlated differently.

For a general worksheet, sum each cohort’s requests per second times prompt length times one minus the skipped fraction, then divide by the assumed effective capacity and round up. Multiplying the global mean length by the average remaining fraction is exact when prompt length and skipped fraction have zero request-weighted covariance. That means their average product equals the product of their averages. Equal hit and miss mean lengths suffice for this two-group worksheet. Measure uncached work directly when that simplification fails.

Routing also weighs locality, isolation and approved region. With the earlier supplied service terms, cold finishes after its queue q plus ninety-six milliseconds. Warm finishes after q plus extra wait delta plus thirty-five. The shared q cancels. Warm saves sixty-one milliseconds of service, so more than sixty-one extra queue milliseconds reverses its advantage; equality is a tie.

Eligibility comes first: authenticated scope, current model, residency and capacity must permit the route. A nearby region cannot override a data-residency rule. Reuse affinity is a preference under queue pressure, not a permanent pin. Compare complete eligible routes and keep the editor’s freshness gate even when the faster route changes.

Continuous batching lets requests join and leave active model work; waiting for a fixed batch can delay the first token. Paged KV storage manages physical blocks while the scheduler still needs suitable input and output budgets. More utilization can accompany worse editor queueing, so compare TTFT, edit-to-paint and throughput on the actual cancellable mix.

vLLM and SGLang are engine candidates whose installed contracts need checking. The current Hugging Face page labels TGI maintenance mode and points future work toward newer engines. That dated status is not a benchmark ranking. Count admitted cancelled work and ignored suggestions in cost, and measure cost per useful retained result with the same quality and shown-rate policy.

The executed redactor recognizes only the fictional demo_api_token pattern. Before upload, it replaces the match with API_KEY one and retains the placeholder-to-secret mapping locally. A preexisting API_KEY placeholder raises the fixture’s collision error before any replacement. Reject this fixture before upload and leave the original source unchanged for local review. The detector is deliberately incomplete; production policy also needs coverage tests, upload controls and restricted logging.

Returned placeholder text remains visible for local review. Never automatically restore a secret into arbitrary model-chosen output. Source comments and retrieved files are untrusted context, not authority to widen upload permissions or read another repository. A shared prompt cache must honor the same authenticated scope as ingestion.

The audit helper copies tenant, model and latency bucket and excludes the prompt. It assumes those identifiers were validated upstream and the latency bucket came from an allowlist. The helper performs neither check. The field allowlist establishes that function’s fields, not end-to-end privacy. Proxy logs, exceptions, tracing, crash dumps and SDKs need separate inspection. Frozen inference weights do not enforce a no-training contract; downstream collection and training exports also need controls.

A private VPC, self-hosted service or fully offline deployment can satisfy different source-upload policies. In an air-gapped design, context engine, model and inference server stay local. Moving the boundary does not remove repository identity, network rules, logs, supply-chain checks or model licensing. A private endpoint alone does not establish all of those controls.

State what source may be uploaded, retained or used for training, and apply the policy across telemetry, batches, caches and recovery paths. Shared device batches can be compatible with isolation if actual per-request boundaries and observability are tested; otherwise partition until that evidence exists. An ordinary redacted prompt is still governed proprietary context.

A suggestion can match public code. The current GitHub documentation describes blocking or showing reference information according to account or organization policy. Its public index is limited to public GitHub repositories and periodic refresh; missing a match is not proof of original provenance or license clearance. Keep review and attribution decisions with the actual accepted artifact.

Understanding remains separate from persistence. A completion may invent an API, use a deprecated call or preserve an insecure permission check that the developer leaves in place. Public-code matching does not establish correctness, and a retained span does not establish review. Require relevant tests and security reasoning for the proposed authorization helper before it becomes trusted application behavior.

For stale suggestions, inspect immediate invalidation, late replies and both insertion gates. For slow exact members, inspect local semantic availability before spending GPU time. For fitted code that conflicts below the caret, inspect suffix preservation and the checkpoint’s infill interface. A nearest-header string cannot certify scope. Each symptom names a smaller state boundary to test.

For poor cache hits, compare actual leading IDs, adapter and policy scope, eviction and replica placement before enforcing affinity. For latency spikes, separate queue, context, prefill, decode and debounce. For apparent acceptance gains, inspect shown population and retained text. Change one causal lever on a fixed replay and preserve the original editor snapshot in the report.

The completion path now knows which requests can stay local, what context a generated insertion needs, and when a returned suggestion has become stale. Its budget includes the user’s waiting time. Its quality report checks what developers retained as well as what they briefly accepted.

Build those contracts around the model before optimizing its serving kernels. Test out-of-order replies, cursor-only changes, upload-policy changes and acceptance races alongside code quality. Then a fast suggestion can remain a useful proposed edit at the exact place the developer is working.

No. The old request epoch still differs, and neither move submitted a replacement request or explicitly rebased the old proposal. Returning to a visible position does not undo invalidation. The useful artifact is a proposed edit whose context, computation, policy and measurement still belong to its current owner. Preserve the same buffer and immutable response identities while repairing the earliest failed boundary. These local contract checks earned the gate logic; an actual editor, model and serving replay must earn product latency and code quality separately. The multi-tenant platform next shares compatible model work while keeping each reader’s evidence, request state, allowance and usage records inside its own boundary.
